findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0364: Exported And Unprotected Activities That Expose Sensitive Functionality
findings.explanation:
Exported activities from *-internal modules and app/src/internal ship only in the internal flavor (internalImplementation). Release exports are browser entry points (IntentDispatcher, BrowserActivity, SystemSearch, SelectedText*, Settings, NewTabSettings); BrowserActivity is exported without a filter and its extra handling needs manual review. Ward's analyzer said: Exported activities without a permission. Ward lists them; check whether each one exposes sensitive functionality or trusts its intent's data.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0326: References to APIs Allowing Fallback to Non-Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
Access to saved passwords is gated by BiometricPrompt allowing DEVICE_CREDENTIAL (and setDeviceCredentialAllowed on API 28-29), i.e. fallback to PIN/pattern for sensitive data. Hardening-level weakness.
autofill/autofill-impl/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/autofill/impl/deviceauth/AuthLauncher.kt:149: Allowed authenticators include DEVICE_CREDENTIAL.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0327: References to APIs for Event-Bound Biometric Authentication
findings.explanation:
BiometricPrompt.authenticate is called without a CryptoObject for password-manager and Sync access, and no key is generated with setUserAuthenticationRequired(true); success is purely event-bound (onAuthenticationSucceeded).
autofill/autofill-impl/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/autofill/impl/deviceauth/AuthLauncher.kt:77: authenticate() without CryptoObject guards saved passwords.
sync/sync-impl/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/sync/impl/auth/AuthLauncher.kt:76: authenticate() without CryptoObject guards Sync actions.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0393: Use of Unverified App Links
findings.explanation:
IntentDispatcherActivity declares http/https VIEW+BROWSABLE filters without autoVerify, but they have no host: this is the generic default-browser registration, not an App Link claiming a domain, so verification does not apply in the usual sense. Needs a human call.
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:294: Host-less https scheme in a browser intent filter without autoVerify.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0399: SafeBrowsing Disabled
findings.explanation:
The manifest sets android.webkit.WebView.EnableSafeBrowsing to false for all WebViews (the app relies on its own malicious-site protection instead).
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:92: SafeBrowsing meta-data is declared...
app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:93: ...and set to false.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0235: Android App Configurations Allowing Cleartext Traffic
findings.explanation:
The network security config's base-config permits cleartext traffic for every domain.
app/src/fdroid/res/xml/network_security_config.xml:26: base-config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0283: Incorrect Implementation of Server Hostname Verification
findings.explanation:
No HostnameVerifier is used, but the WebView SSL-error fallback trusts a certificate once its signature chain reaches a bundled Let's Encrypt root, without checking that the leaf matches the hostname or is within validity. A mismatched-host cert that also triggers SSL_UNTRUSTED can therefore be accepted.
app/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/app/browser/certificates/rootstore/TrustedCertificateStore.kt:66: Validation only looks up the issuer by CN and verifies signatures; no hostname or leaf-validity check.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0284: Incorrect SSL Error Handling in WebViews
findings.explanation:
onReceivedSslError decides only on getPrimaryError(): when it is SSL_UNTRUSTED and the chain verifies to a bundled Let's Encrypt root, it calls proceed() without checking other errors (SSL_IDMISMATCH, SSL_EXPIRED) via hasError(). The same pattern is in the URL-extraction WebView.
app/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/app/browser/BrowserWebViewClient.kt:1006: Decision based solely on the primary SSL error.
app/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/app/browser/BrowserWebViewClient.kt:1017: proceed() after the partial chain check.
app/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/app/browser/urlextraction/UrlExtractingWebViewClient.kt:135: Same proceed() pattern in the URL-extraction WebView.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0372: Implicit Intents Used for Internal App Communication
findings.explanation:
Internal VPN call-state actions are sent as implicit broadcasts with no package or permission, so any app can register a receiver for these actions.
network-protection/network-protection-impl/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/networkprotection/impl/snooze/VpnDisableOnCall.kt:52: Implicit broadcast for an app-internal action.
network-protection/network-protection-impl/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/networkprotection/impl/snooze/VpnDisableOnCall.kt:58: Implicit broadcast for an app-internal action.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0316: App Exposing User Authentication Data in Text Input Fields
findings.explanation:
DaxTextInput in password mode reveals the password (transformationMethod null, VISIBLE_PASSWORD) whenever the field gains focus, so password entry, e.g. the HTTP authentication dialog, is unmasked while typing.
android-design-system/design-system/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/common/ui/view/text/DaxTextInput.kt:180: On focus, password fields call showPassword(), which removes masking.
app/src/main/res/layout/http_authentication.xml:44: HTTP auth password entry uses this DaxTextInput password type.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0202: References to APIs and Permissions for Accessing External Storage
findings.explanation:
WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is declared (maxSdkVersion 29) and Duck.ai chat export writes the full chat text/zip unencrypted to the public Downloads folder. It is a user-initiated export, so whether this counts as unintended sensitive-data exposure needs a human decision. The Sync recovery-code PDF goes to cacheDir (internal), not shared storage.
duckchat/duckchat-impl/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/duckchat/impl/history/ChatExportWriter.kt:68: Chat export is written in plaintext to the shared public Downloads directory.

findings.title: MASTG-TEST-0231: References to Logging APIs
findings.explanation:
Release code logs the Email Protection personal access token and the PIR JS-bridge secret via logcat{}. Output reaches Logcat only when a logger is installed (debuggable build or the AppTP verboseLogging toggle), but the sensitive values are passed to the logging API in release code.
app/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/app/email/sync/EmailSync.kt:93: Email Protection username and personal access token are interpolated into a log message.
pir/pir-impl/src/main/java/com/duckduckgo/pir/impl/scripts/PirMessagingInterface.kt:75: JS bridge message and its shared secret are logged.
